question:
A company models revenue for selling $x$ items as $R(x) = 70x-0.5x^2$, and cost as $C(x) = 10x+600$.

(a) Express profit $P(x)$ as a function.

(b) Find the $x$ maximizing profit.

(c) Test the nature using both first and second derivatives.
explanation:
(a) $P(x) = R(x)-C(x) = 60x-0.5x^2-600$

(b) $P'(x)=60-x$, so $x=60$.

$P''(x)=-1<0$, confirming maximum.

(c) First derivative changes sign from positive to negative at $x=60$.

options.A:
(a) $P(x)=80x-0.5x^2+600$
(b) Profit is maximized at $x=80$.
(c) $P''(x)=1>0$, so it gives a minimum.
options.B:
(a) $P(x)=60x+0.5x^2-600$
(b) Profit is maximized at $x=60$.
(c) First derivative changes sign from negative to positive at $x=60$.
options.C:
(a) $P(x)=60x-0.5x^2-600$
(b) Profit is maximized at $x=60$.
(c) $P''(x)=-1<0$, and $P'(x)$ changes sign from positive to negative at $x=60$.
options.D:
(a) $P(x)=70x-0.5x^2-600$
(b) Profit is maximized at $x=70$.
(c) $P''(x)=0$, so the test is inconclusive.
